Inspect Steward is a system for automated execution and supervision of long-running evaluations. Steward enables you to launch a large run and walk away while a coding agent monitors it and automatically intervenes when required. 

- Evaluation runs are fully unattended by design, but can escalate to humans when required.
- Opinionated defaults for error handling keep tasks running, with an agent driven workflow for error resolution and retry.
- Slack notifications to keep operators apprised of status and pending decisions.
- Works with `eval_set()` as well as with execution frameworks like [Inspect Flow](https://meridianlabs-ai.github.io/inspect_flow/) and [Inspect Hawk](https://hawk.metr.org).
::::


## Quick Tour

First, install Steward from GitHub with:

```bash
pip install git+https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_steward
```

To use Steward, create a directory, switch to it, then call `steward init`:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/runs/swe-evals
cd ~/runs/swe-evals
steward init
```

This will scaffold up a Steward workspace with an `evalset.py` and `AGENTS.md` file that teaches the agent how to use Steward to run an evaluation. First, define your eval set:

```{.python filename="evalset.py"}
from inspect_ai import eval_set
from inspect_harbor import cais_swebenchpro, datacurve_deep_swe

eval_set(
    tasks=[cais_swebenchpro(),  datacurve_deep_swe()],
    model=["openai/gpt-5.6-sol", "anthropic/claude-opus-5"],
    log_dir="logs/swe-evals"
)
```

Steward can manage any evalution defined with a script that ends in a call to `eval_set()` or alternatively a `flow.py` from [Flow](https://meridianlabs-ai.github.io/inspect_flow/) or a `hawk.yaml` from [Hawk](https://hawk.metr.org).


Next, launch your coding agent from the workspace and tell it to run the evaluation (you should typically run from a [tmux](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/wiki) detached terminal so the agent is persistent):

```bash
$ claude
───────────────────────────────────────────── swe-evals ─
❯ please run this evaluation.
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

The agent will launch all of the tasks, setup a background monitoring process, and respond to alerts that require its intervention. From here you can detach and walk away. The run depends on neither you nor the agent staying connected. When you come back, ask how it's going:

```bash
───────────────────────────────────────────── swe-evals ─
❯ how is the eval going?
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

The agent reports where the run stands: per-task progress, what it resolved on its own while you were gone, and anything that is waiting on a decision from you.

::: {.callout-note}
#### Notifications

We strongly recommend you also configure [Inspect Notifications](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/intervention.html#notifications) by setting an `INSPECT_EVAL_NOTIFICATION` environment variable. For example in your `.env` file:

```{.ini}
INSPECT_EVAL_NOTIFICATION=slack://{OAuthToken}/
```
:::

## Eval Workflow

An evaluation run moves through five phases. The agent drives all of them; you
make the decisions that require a person. In practice the middle phases
overlap: errors are investigated while the eval is running, and scanning
starts as tasks complete.


| Phase | Description |
|----|----|
| Smoke | `steward launch --smoke` rehearses the eval set with a few samples per task under a time cap, catching configuration and environment problems before the full run. |
| Eval | The full run: one process per task, with progress reported on a schedule. Tasks that fail outright are re-launched (up to `stall_after` attempts); sample errors don't halt a task and are collected for later review. If a task is waiting on human input (e.g. a tool call approval) you are notified. |
| Scanning | As tasks complete, Steward scans transcripts for problems that scores don't surface (refusals scored as failures, environment misconfiguration, evaluation awareness). Findings are written to `scanning.md`. |
| Investigation | Errors and scan findings are grouped into classes for review. The agent investigates each class, then acts within your standing policy or asks you. Decisions are recorded as they happen; the agent's writeup lands in `analysis.md`. |
| Signoff | `steward signoff` records that you accept the results, unschedules the background monitor, and archives superseded logs. The one command the agent may never run. |
: {tbl-colwidths="[20,80]"}

However, evaluation runs don't always proceed without a hitch! Steward has several pieces of agent-driven workflow to help work through issues that can arise. For example:

- Steward automatically continues tasks even where there are sample errors. You
  will then need to decide how to handle these errors (re-run them, score them
  as failed, exclude them from scoring, etc.) and the agent carries out your
  decision.

- When a task fails outright (for example, an import error or an out-of-memory
  crash) Steward re-launches it a limited number of times, then stops and
  reports it rather than spending money on retries that won't succeed.

- The agent groups errors into classes (rate limits, sandbox failures, a scorer
  bug) so that you can make one decision about a hundred samples rather than a
  hundred decisions.

- If a task is waiting on human input (for example, a tool call approval)
  Steward notifies you and the task holds its place in the run until you
  respond.

- You can change the eval set mid-run: edit your definition and launch again,
  and Steward runs only what is new or changed. Completed work is never re-run.

The agent will notify you when any of these conditions exist and will help you resolve them as required.

## Steward Options

Steward writes a `_steward.yaml` file to your workspace which can be used to tune the behavior of the monitor and agent. The settings at the top are what Steward acts on by itself; `policies` is free-form text the agent consults when making decisions. For example:

```{.yaml filename="_steward.yaml"}
tend_interval: 10m
stall_after: 3
max_workers: 8

policies:
  - If more than 10% of the samples in a task error out, pause the run
    and notify me right away. Otherwise, batch up questions for the end
    of the run.
  - A re-run that would replay more than 200 samples needs my approval
    first.
  - If a task's score looks implausible (e.g. near zero on a task that
    usually scores well), investigate the transcripts before proposing
    a re-run.
```

See the [Workspace](workspace.qmd) article for details on all available options.
